sanskrit: dhruvaṃ vai brāhmaṇe satyaṃ dhruvā sādhuṣu saṃnatiḥ śrīr dhruvā cāpi dakṣeṣu dhruvo nārāyaṇe jayaḥ
english: Truth dwells assured in the Brāhmaṇa, humility assured in the good, prosperity assured in the able, and victory assured in Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evam uktvā hṛṣīkeśaṃ svayam ātmānam ātmanā saṃdideśārjuno nardan vāsaviḥ keśavaṃ prabhum
english: Saṃjaya said: Having spoken thus to Hṛṣīkeśa, Arjuna, the son of Vāsava, roaring aloud, charged his own self by his own resolve and addressed the lord Keśava.

sanskrit: yathā prabhātāṃ rajanīṃ kalpitaḥ syād ratho mama tathā kāryaṃ tvayā kṛṣṇa kāryaṃ hi mahad udyatam
english: "When night has brightened into dawn, let my chariot be made ready. So must you act, Kṛṣṇa, for a great deed is now undertaken."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tāṃ niśāṃ duḥkhaśokārtau śvasantāv iva coragau nidrāṃ naivopalebhāte vāsudevadhanaṃjayau
english: Saṃjaya said: Through that night Vāsudeva and Dhanaṃjaya, stricken with grief and sorrow, hissing like serpents, found no sleep at all.

sanskrit: naranārāyaṇau kruddhau jñātvā devāḥ savāsavāḥ vyathitāś cintayām āsuḥ kiṃ svid etad bhaviṣyati
english: Knowing Nara and Nārāyaṇa to be enraged, the gods together with Vāsava grew troubled and pondered: "What now is to come of this?"

sanskrit: vavuś ca dāruṇā vātā rūkṣā gorābhiśaṃsinaḥ sakabandhas tathāditye parighaḥ samadṛśyata
english: Harsh and savage winds blew, foreboding terror, and across the face of the sun there was seen a headless trunk and an iron bar.

sanskrit: śuṣkāśanyaś ca niṣpetuḥ sanirghātāḥ savidyutaḥ cacāla cāpi pṛthivī saśailavanakānanā
english: Dry thunderbolts fell with crashing peals and lightning, and the earth trembled with its mountains, woods, and forests.

sanskrit: cukṣubhuś ca mahārāja sāgarā makarālayāḥ pratisrotaḥ pravṛttāś ca tathā gantuṃ samudragāḥ
english: The oceans, abodes of sea-monsters, were churned into uproar, great king, and the rivers that flow to the sea began to run backward against their current.

sanskrit: rathāśvanaranāgānāṃ pravṛttam adharottaram kravyādānāṃ pramodārthaṃ yamarāṣṭravivṛddhaye
english: Chariots, horses, men, and elephants were turned upside down, for the delight of the flesh-eaters and the swelling of Yama's realm.

sanskrit: vāhanāni śakṛnmūtre mumucū ruruduś ca ha tān dṛṣṭvā dāruṇān sarvān utpātāṃl lomaharṣaṇān
english: The draught-animals let fall their dung and urine and wept aloud; and beholding all these dreadful, hair-raising portents—

sanskrit: sarve te vyathitāḥ sainyās tvadīyā bharatarṣabha śrutvā mahābalasyogrāṃ pratijñāṃ savyasācinaḥ
english: —all your troops were filled with dismay, O bull of the Bhāratas, hearing the fierce vow of the mighty Savyasācin.

sanskrit: atha kṛṣṇaṃ mahābāhur abravīt pākaśāsaniḥ āśvāsaya subhadrāṃ tvaṃ bhaginīṃ snuṣayā saha
english: Then the mighty-armed son of the Chastiser of Pāka said to Kṛṣṇa: "Console your sister Subhadrā, and her daughter-in-law with her."

sanskrit: snuṣā śvaśvrānaghāyaste viśoke kuru mādhava sāmnā satyena yuktena vacasāśvāsaya prabho
english: "Set the daughter-in-law and her mother-in-law, the blameless ones, free of grief, Mādhava; with gentle, true, and fitting words console them, O lord."

sanskrit: tato 'rjunagṛhaṃ gatvā vāsudevaḥ sudurmanāḥ bhaginīṃ putraśokārtām āśvāsayata duḥkhitām
english: Then Vāsudeva, sore at heart, went to Arjuna's dwelling and consoled his grieving sister, stricken with sorrow for her son.

sanskrit: mā śokaṃ kuru vārṣṇeyi kumāraṃ prati sasnuṣā sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ bhīru niṣṭhaiṣā kālanirmitā
english: "Grieve not for the boy, daughter of the Vṛṣṇis, you and your daughter-in-law; for all living beings, O timid one, this is the end appointed by Time."

sanskrit: kule jatasya vīrasya kṣatriyasya viśeṣataḥ sadṛśaṃ maraṇaṃ hy etat tava putrasya mā śucaḥ
english: "For a hero born in a noble line, and most of all a Kṣatriya, such a death is befitting; grieve not for your son."

sanskrit: diṣṭyā mahāratho vīraḥ pitus tulyaparākramaḥ kṣātreṇa vidhinā prāpto vīrābhilaṣitāṃ gatim
english: "By good fortune the heroic great warrior, equal in valor to his father, has by the law of the Kṣatriyas attained the goal that heroes long for."

sanskrit: jitvā subahuśaḥ śatrūn preṣayitvā ca mṛtyave gataḥ puṇyakṛtāṃ lokān sarvakāmaduho 'kṣayān
english: "Having conquered foes in great numbers and sent them to their death, he has gone to the imperishable worlds of the doers of good, that yield every desire."

sanskrit: tapasā brahmacaryeṇa śrutena prajñayāpi ca santo yāṃ gatim icchanti prāptas tāṃ tava putrakaḥ
english: "That goal which the good seek through austerity, through chastity, through sacred learning and through wisdom—that goal your son has attained."

sanskrit: vīrasūr vīrapatnī tvaṃ vīraśvaśurabāndhavā mā śucas tanayaṃ bhadre gataḥ sa paramāṃ gatim
english: "You are the mother of a hero, the wife of a hero, kinswoman to heroic fathers-in-law; grieve not for your son, good lady, for he has gone to the highest goal."

sanskrit: prāpsyate cāpy asau kṣudraḥ saindhavo bālaghātakaḥ asyāvalepasya phalaṃ sasuhṛdgaṇabāndhavaḥ
english: "And that base Saindhava, the slayer of a boy, shall reap the fruit of his insolence, he together with his band of friends and kinsmen."

sanskrit: vyuṣṭāyāṃ tu varārohe rajanyāṃ pāpakarmakṛt na hi mokṣyati pārthāt sa praviṣṭo 'py amarāvatīm
english: "When the night has passed, O fair-hipped one, that doer of evil deeds shall not escape Pārtha, even though he enter Amarāvatī itself."

sanskrit: śvaḥ śiraḥ śroṣyase tasya saindhavasya raṇe hṛtam samantapañcakād bāhyaṃ viśokā bhava mā rudaḥ
english: "Tomorrow you shall hear that the head of that Saindhava has been struck off in battle, cast beyond Samantapañcaka. Be free of grief; weep not."

sanskrit: kṣatradharmaṃ puraskṛtya gataḥ śūraḥ satāṃ gatim yāṃ vayaṃ prāpnuyāmeha ye cānye śastrajīvinaḥ
english: "Holding the law of the Kṣatriya foremost, the hero has gone to the goal of the good—the goal which we too may attain, and others who live by the sword."

sanskrit: vyūḍhorasko mahābāhur anivartī varapraṇut gatas tava varārohe putraḥ svargaṃ jvaraṃ jahi
english: "Broad-chested, mighty-armed, never turning back, humbler of the foremost foes—your son, O fair-hipped one, has gone to heaven. Cast off your fever of grief."

sanskrit: anu jātaś ca pitaraṃ mātṛpakṣaṃ ca vīryavān sahasraśo ripūn hatvā hataḥ śūro mahārathaḥ
english: "Taking after his father and his mother's line, the valiant one, having slain enemies by the thousand, the heroic great warrior was himself slain."

sanskrit: āśvāsaya snuṣāṃ rājñi mā śucaḥ kṣatriye bhṛṣam śvaḥ priyaṃ sumahac chrutvā viśokā bhava nandini
english: "Console your daughter-in-law, O lady; grieve not so deeply, O Kṣatriya woman. Tomorrow, hearing tidings most welcome and great, you shall be free of grief, O joyful one."

sanskrit: yat pārthena pratijñātaṃ tat tathā na tad anyathā cikīrṣitaṃ hi te bhartur na bhavej jātu niṣphalam
english: "What Pārtha has vowed shall be so and not otherwise; for what your brother resolves to do can never come to nothing."

sanskrit: yadi ca manujapannagāḥ piśācā; rajanicarāḥ patagāḥ surāsurāś ca raṇagatam abhiyānti sindhurājaṃ; na sa bhavitā saha tair api prabhāte
english: "Even if men and serpents, demons, night-rovers, and birds, gods and antigods, should rush to the side of the king of Sindhu in battle, he shall be no more, nor they with him, when morning comes."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca etac chrutvā vacas tasya keśavasya mahātmanaḥ subhadrā putraśokārtā vilalāpa suduḥkhitā
english: Saṃjaya said: Having heard these words of the great-souled Keśava, Subhadrā, stricken with grief for her son and sorely afflicted, lamented aloud.

sanskrit: hā putra mama mandāyāḥ kathaṃ saṃyugam etya ha nidhanaṃ prāptavāṃs tāta pitṛtulyaparākramaḥ
english: "Alas, my son! How is it that, going into battle, you who were equal to your father in valor have met your end, dear child, son of luckless me?"

sanskrit: katham indīvaraśyāmaṃ sudaṃṣṭraṃ cārulocanam mukhaṃ te dṛśyate vatsa guṇṭhitaṃ raṇareṇunā
english: "How is it that your face, dark as the blue lotus, with fine teeth and lovely eyes, is now seen, my darling, veiled in the dust of battle?"

sanskrit: nūnaṃ śūraṃ nipatitaṃ tvāṃ paśyanty anivartinam suśirogrīvabāhvaṃsaṃ vyūḍhoraskaṃ nirūdaram
english: "Surely they now look upon you, the hero fallen, who never turned back—fair of head, neck, arms, and shoulders, broad-chested, lean of belly—"

sanskrit: cārūpacitasarvāṅgaṃ svakṣaṃ śastrakṣatācitam bhūtāni tvā nirīkṣante nūnaṃ candram ivoditam
english: "—every limb beautifully formed, fair-eyed, strewn with weapon-wounds; surely the creatures gaze upon you as upon the risen moon."

sanskrit: śayanīyaṃ purā yasya spardhyāstaraṇasaṃvṛtam bhūmāv adya kathaṃ śeṣe vipraviddhaḥ sukhocitaḥ
english: "You whose couch was once spread with coverlets to be envied—how do you lie today upon the bare ground, flung down, you who were used to comfort?"

sanskrit: yo 'nvāsyata purā vīro varastrībhir mahābhujaḥ katham anvāsyate so 'dya śivābhiḥ patito mṛdhe
english: "The hero, mighty-armed, once waited upon by the loveliest of women—how is it that he, fallen in battle, is today waited upon by jackals?"

sanskrit: yo 'stūyata purā hṛṣṭaiḥ sūtamāgadhabandibhiḥ so 'dya kravyādgaṇair ghorair vinadadbhir upāsyate
english: "He who was once praised by joyful bards, heralds, and minstrels is today attended by dreadful, howling packs of flesh-eaters."

sanskrit: pāṇḍaveṣu ca nātheṣu vṛṣṇivīreṣu cābhibho pāñcāleṣu ca vīreṣu hataḥ kenāsy anāthavat
english: "With the Pāṇḍavas for your protectors, O mighty one, and the heroes of the Vṛṣṇis and the heroes of the Pāñcālas—by whom were you slain, as though you had no protector at all?"

sanskrit: atṛptadarśanā putra darśanasya tavānagha mandabhāgyā gamiṣyāmi vyaktam adya yamakṣayam
english: "Never sated with the sight of you, my blameless son, I, ill-fated, shall surely go today to the realm of Yama."

sanskrit: viśālākṣaṃ sukeśāntaṃ cāruvākyaṃ sugandhi ca tava putra kadā bhūyo mukhaṃ drakṣyāmi nirvraṇam
english: "Wide-eyed, fair-haired at the temples, sweet of speech and fragrant—when, my son, shall I look again upon your unwounded face?"

sanskrit: dhig balaṃ bhīmasenasya dhik pārthasya dhanuṣmatām dhig vīryaṃ vṛṣṇivīrāṇāṃ pāñcālānāṃ ca dhig balam
english: "A curse upon the strength of Bhīmasena, a curse upon Pārtha among the bowmen, a curse upon the prowess of the Vṛṣṇi heroes, and a curse upon the might of the Pāñcālas!"

sanskrit: dhik kekayāṃs tathā cedīn matsyāṃś caivātha sṛñjayān ye tvā raṇe gataṃ vīraṃ na jānanti nipātitam
english: "A curse upon the Kekayas, the Cedis, the Matsyas, and the Sṛñjayas, who knew not that you, the hero, had gone into the fray and been struck down."

sanskrit: adya paśyāmi pṛthivīṃ śūnyām iva hatatviṣam abhimanyum apaśyantī śokavyākulalocanā
english: "Today, not seeing Abhimanyu, with eyes troubled by grief, I behold the earth as if empty, its splendor put out."

sanskrit: svasrīyaṃ vāsudevasya putraṃ gāṇḍīvadhanvanaḥ kathaṃ tvā virathaṃ vīraṃ drakṣyāmy anyair nipātitam
english: "Sister's son of Vāsudeva, son of the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva—how shall I look upon you, the hero, robbed of your chariot and brought down by others?"

sanskrit: hā vīra dṛṣṭo naṣṭaś ca dhanaṃ svapna ivāsi me aho hy anityaṃ mānuṣyaṃ jalabudbudacañcalam
english: "Alas, hero, seen and then lost, you are to me like wealth in a dream! Ah, how fleeting is human life, unsteady as a bubble on the water!"

sanskrit: imāṃ te taruṇīṃ bhāryāṃ tvadādhibhir abhiplutām kathaṃ saṃdhārayiṣyāmi vivatsām iva dhenukām
english: "This your young wife, overwhelmed with grief for you—how shall I sustain her, like a cow bereft of her calf?"

sanskrit: aho hy akāle prasthānaṃ kṛtavān asi putraka vihāya phalakāle māṃ sugṛddhāṃ tava darśane
english: "Ah, you have set forth out of season, my little son, forsaking me—who longed so to see you—at the very time of harvest."

sanskrit: nūnaṃ gatiḥ kṛtāntasya prājñair api sudurvidā yatra tvaṃ keśave nāthe saṃgrāme 'nāthavad dhataḥ
english: "Surely the course of Fate is hard to fathom even for the wise, since you, with Keśava for your protector, were slain in battle as though protectorless."

sanskrit: yajvanāṃ dānaśīlānāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ kṛtātmanām caritabrahmacaryāṇāṃ puṇyatīrthāvagāhinām
english: "That goal which belongs to performers of sacrifice, to the charitable, to the Brāhmaṇas of perfected souls, to those who have kept the vow of chastity and have bathed at holy fords—"

sanskrit: kṛtajñānāṃ vadānyānāṃ guruśuśrūṣiṇām api sahasradakṣiṇānāṃ ca yā gatis tām avāpnuhi
english: "—to the grateful, the generous, those devoted to the service of their elders, and those who give the thousandfold sacrificial fee—that goal may you attain."

sanskrit: yā gatir yudhyamānānāṃ śūrāṇām anivartinām hatvārīn nihatānāṃ ca saṃgrāme tāṃ gatiṃ vraja
english: "That goal which belongs to heroes fighting on and never turning back, who slay their foes and are themselves slain in battle—to that goal go."

sanskrit: gosahasrapradātṝṇāṃ kratudānāṃ ca yā gatiḥ naiveśikaṃ cābhimataṃ dadatāṃ yā gatiḥ śubhā
english: "That goal which is the givers' of a thousand cows and of the offerings of sacrifice, that blessed goal of those who bestow a cherished dwelling—"

sanskrit: brahmacaryeṇa yāṃ yānti munayaḥ saṃśitavratā ekapatnyaś ca yāṃ yānti tāṃ gatiṃ vraja putraka
english: "—that goal which sages of strict vows reach through chastity, and which faithful wives of a single husband reach—to that goal go, my little son."

sanskrit: rājñāṃ sucaritair yā ca gatir bhavati śāśvatī caturāśramiṇāṃ puṇyaiḥ pāvitānāṃ surakṣitaiḥ
english: "That everlasting goal which comes to kings by their good conduct, and to those of the four life-stages, purified and well-guarded by their meritorious deeds—"

sanskrit: dīnānukampināṃ yā ca satataṃ saṃvibhāginām paiśunyāc ca nivṛttānāṃ tāṃ gatiṃ vraja putraka
english: "—that goal of those who pity the wretched, who ever share what they have, and who have turned away from slander—to that goal go, my little son."

sanskrit: vratināṃ dharmaśīlānāṃ guruśuśrūṣiṇām api amoghātithināṃ yā ca tāṃ gatiṃ vraja putraka
english: "That goal of those true to their vows, of righteous nature, devoted to the service of their elders, who never turn a guest away in vain—to that goal go, my little son."

sanskrit: ṛtukāle svakāṃ patnīṃ gacchatāṃ yā manasvinām na cānyadārasevīnāṃ tāṃ gatiṃ vraja putraka
english: "That goal of the high-minded who go to their own wives only in the proper season and never resort to the wives of others—to that goal go, my little son."

sanskrit: sāmnā ye sarvabhūtāni gacchanti gatamatsarāḥ nāruṃtudānāṃ kṣamiṇāṃ yā gatis tām avāpnuhi
english: "That goal of those, free from envy, who approach all beings with gentleness, who wound no one and are forbearing—that goal may you attain."

sanskrit: madhumāṃsanivṛttānāṃ madād dambhāt tathānṛtāt paropatāpatyaktānāṃ tāṃ gatiṃ vraja putraka
english: "That goal of those who abstain from wine and flesh, who have renounced pride, hypocrisy, and falsehood, and the tormenting of others—to that goal go, my little son."

sanskrit: hrīmantaḥ sarvaśāstrajñā jñānatṛptā jitendriyāḥ yāṃ gatiṃ sādhavo yānti tāṃ gatiṃ vraja putraka
english: "That goal which the good attain—the modest, the masters of all the scriptures, content in knowledge, with senses subdued—to that goal go, my little son."

sanskrit: evaṃ vilapatīṃ dīnāṃ subhadrāṃ śokakarśitām abhyapadyata pāñcālī vairāṭīsahitā tadā
english: As Subhadrā lamented thus, forlorn and wasted with grief, the Pāñcāla princess, together with Virāṭa's daughter, then came to her side.

sanskrit: tāḥ prakāmaṃ ruditvā ca vilapya ca suduḥkhitāḥ unmattavat tadā rājan visaṃjñā nyapatan kṣitau
english: Having wept their fill and lamented in deep distress, those women, like ones gone mad, fell senseless to the ground, O king.

sanskrit: sopacāras tu kṛṣṇas tāṃ duḥkhitāṃ bhṛśaduḥkhitaḥ siktvāmbhasā samāśvāsya tat tad uktvā hitaṃ vacaḥ
english: But Kṛṣṇa, himself sorely grieved, tended to her in her sorrow, sprinkling water upon her and reviving her, speaking now this, now that, kindly word.

sanskrit: visaṃjñakalpāṃ rudatīm apaviddhāṃ pravepatīm bhaginīṃ puṇḍarīkākṣa idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: To his sister—well-nigh senseless, weeping, fallen prostrate and trembling—the lotus-eyed one spoke these words:

sanskrit: subhadre mā śucaḥ putraṃ pāñcālyāśvāsayottarām gato 'bhimanyuḥ prathitāṃ gatiṃ kṣatriyapuṃgavaḥ
english: "Subhadrā, grieve not for your son; with the Pāñcāla princess console Uttarā. Abhimanyu, that bull among Kṣatriyas, has gone to the renowned goal."

sanskrit: ye cānye 'pi kule santi puruṣā no varānane sarve te vai gatiṃ yāntu abhimanyor yaśasvinaḥ
english: "And whatever other men there are in our line, O fair-faced one—may they all attain the goal of the glorious Abhimanyu."

sanskrit: kuryāma tad vayaṃ karma kriyāsuḥ suhṛdaś ca naḥ kṛtavān yādṛg adyaikas tava putro mahārathaḥ
english: "May we, and our friends as well, perform such a deed as your son, the lone great warrior, has wrought this day."

sanskrit: evam āśvāsya bhaginīṃ draupadīm api cottarām pārthasyaiva mahābāhuḥ pārśvam āgād ariṃdamaḥ
english: Having thus consoled his sister, and Draupadī and Uttarā as well, the mighty-armed subduer of foes returned to Pārtha's side.

sanskrit: tato 'bhyanujñāya nṛpān kṛṣṇo bandhūṃs tathābhibhūḥ viveśāntaḥpuraṃ rājaṃs te 'nye jagmur yathālayam
english: Then the lord Kṛṣṇa, taking leave of the kings and the kinsmen, entered the inner apartments, O king, while the others went each to his own quarters.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato 'rjunasya bhavanaṃ praviśyāpratimaṃ vibhuḥ spṛṣṭvāmbhaḥ puṇḍarīkākṣaḥ sthaṇḍile śubhalakṣaṇe saṃtastāra śubhāṃ śayyāṃ darbhair vaiḍūryasaṃnibhaiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then the lotus-eyed lord entered Arjuna's peerless dwelling, and having touched water, spread upon an auspiciously marked patch of cleared ground a fair bed of darbha grasses that gleamed like beryl.

sanskrit: tato mālyena vidhival lājair gandhaiḥ sumaṅgalaiḥ alaṃcakāra tāṃ śayyāṃ parivāryāyudhottamaiḥ
english: Then with garlands, duly with parched grain and sweet auspicious perfumes, he adorned that bed, ringing it about with the finest weapons.

sanskrit: tataḥ spṛṣṭodakaṃ pārthaṃ vinītāḥ paricārakāḥ darśayāṃ naityakaṃ cakrur naiśaṃ traiyambakaṃ balim
english: Then the well-trained attendants showed to Pārtha, who had touched water, the customary nightly offering to Tryambaka.

sanskrit: tataḥ prītamanāḥ pārtho gandhair mālyaiś ca mādhavam alaṃkṛtyopahāraṃ taṃ naiśam asmai nyavedayat
english: Then Pārtha, glad of heart, adorning Mādhava with perfumes and garlands, presented to him that nightly offering.

sanskrit: smayamānas tu govindaḥ phalgunaṃ pratyabhāṣata supyatāṃ pārtha bhadraṃ te kalyāṇāya vrajāmy aham
english: Govinda, smiling, answered Phalguna: "Let us take our rest, Pārtha; blessings upon you. I go now to ensure your welfare."

sanskrit: sthāpayitvā tato dvāḥsthān goptṝṃś cāttāyudhān narān dārukānugataḥ śrīmān viveśa śibiraṃ svakam śiśye ca śayane śubhre bahukṛtyaṃ vicintayan
english: Then, having posted doorkeepers and armed men as guards, the glorious one, followed by Dāruka, entered his own pavilion and lay down upon a spotless couch, pondering the many tasks at hand.

sanskrit: na pāṇḍavānāṃ śibire kaś cit suṣvāpa tāṃ niśām prajāgaraḥ sarvajanam āviveśa viśāṃ pate
english: In the Pāṇḍavas' camp no one slept that night; wakefulness came over every one of them, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: putraśokābhibhūtena pratijñāto mahātmanā sahasā sindhurājasya vadho gāṇḍīvadhanvanā
english: For the slaying of the king of Sindhu had been vowed in haste by the great-souled wielder of the Gāṇḍīva, overwhelmed with grief for his son.

sanskrit: tat kathaṃ nu mahābāhur vāsaviḥ paravīrahā pratijñāṃ saphalāṃ kuryād iti te samacintayan
english: "How then shall the mighty-armed son of Vāsava, slayer of enemy heroes, make his vow bear fruit?"—thus they pondered together.

sanskrit: kaṣṭaṃ hīdaṃ vyavasitaṃ pāṇḍavena mahātmanā putraśokābhitaptena pratijñā mahatī kṛtā
english: "Grievous indeed is this that the great-souled Pāṇḍava has resolved upon; scorched by grief for his son, he has made a mighty vow."

sanskrit: bhrātaraś cāpi vikrāntā bahulāni balāni ca dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putreṇa sarvaṃ tasmai niveditam
english: "And the valiant brothers too, and the vast hosts—all this has been laid before Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son."
